description: Harden the commit pipeline to prevent library corruption. Add dry-run mode, per-action progress reporting, error recovery, idempotency guards, and the 'Upload edited versions' commit action. The commit screen becomes a careful, transparent process that shows exactly what will happen before it happens, reports each step live, and handles partial failures gracefully.
principles: No silent failures: every Immich API call's result is reported to the user
Idempotent: re-running commit does not duplicate stacks, re-trash already-trashed assets, or re-upload already-uploaded edits
Recoverable: partial failures leave the system in a known state. The user can re-run just the failed actions.
Transparent: the user sees exactly what will happen before clicking Commit
Careful: rejects go to Immich trash (recoverable), not permanent delete. Always soft-delete.
stories: CH-001: Dry-run mode — POST /api/sessions/:id/commit?dryRun=true returns what WOULD happen without executing. Show counts in the commit screen before the user clicks.
CH-002: Per-action progress reporting — commit endpoint streams progress (or returns step-by-step). Frontend shows a live log: 'Trashing 19 rejects... done ✓', 'Writing 15 ratings... done ✓', etc.
CH-003: Idempotency for trash — check if assets are already trashed before attempting DELETE. Track trashed asset IDs in a committed_actions table. Skip already-trashed assets on re-commit.
CH-004: Idempotency for stacks — track which stack groups have been committed (committed_stack_group_id). Skip already-committed groups on re-commit.
CH-005: Idempotency for ratings — ratings are idempotent by nature (PUT is safe to repeat). Track to avoid unnecessary API calls.
CH-006: Idempotency for edited uploads — track uploaded edit asset IDs. Skip already-uploaded edits on re-commit.
CH-007: Error recovery UI — if commit partially fails, show which actions succeeded and which failed. Allow re-running just the failed actions.
CH-008: Commit confirmation dialog — before executing, show a summary of destructive actions ('This will trash 19 photos in Immich. This is recoverable from Immich's trash.') with a confirm button.
CH-009: Session committed state — mark session as committed, record committed_at timestamp, store commit results (counts, errors) for the recent sessions display.
researchNeeded: Immich bulk operations: does DELETE /api/assets handle already-trashed IDs gracefully (no error) or does it fail?
Immich rating writes: does PUT /api/assets/:id with same rating value cause any side effects (updated_at change)?
Immich stack creation: what happens if you POST /api/stacks with assets that are already in a stack? (Merge behavior per the API docs, but need to verify)

schema: db/migrations/004-commit-history.sql adds commit_actions for durable per-action outcomes
commit_runs stores each real commit attempt, selected options, structured result, timestamps, and final status
db/schema.sql remains the complete current schema snapshot
api: POST /api/sessions/:id/commit?dryRun=true returns pending and already-applied counts without calling Immich or writing local state
Real commits return structured per-step succeeded, failed, alreadyApplied, and error details while preserving the existing aggregate counters
Trash, rating, and stack successes are recorded independently so retries send only unfinished work
Edited upload retry safety continues to use the persisted Immich asset ID and uploaded render status established during Feature 3
Concurrent commit requests for the same session are rejected while one is active
Commit option types are validated before preview or execution
frontend: Commit first performs a no-write preview and displays a confirmation state inside the design-handoff summary card
Recoverable trash behavior is called out before confirmation
The confirmation distinguishes pending operations from actions already applied during an earlier partial attempt
Results are presented per action, including skipped completed work and actionable failures
Incomplete commits restore the option controls and expose a Retry action
verification: Regression coverage proves dry-run performs no Immich calls and writes no commit history
Regression coverage forces a partial rating failure after successful trash and stack operations, then proves retry sends only the rating
Existing edited-upload retry, existing-stack, and missing-remote-edit tests continue to pass
Full automated suite passes with 38 tests
Browser validation completed at desktop and 390x844; confirmation and failure/retry states remain usable without horizontal overflow
